# Persistence Analysis {#sec-bem-persistence}

In Chapter 4, @bali2016 measure persistence by correlating a stock characteristic with its own future value across stocks.
We use the December 1988–2012 panel from @sec-summary-statistics, including its signed book-to-market ratio (BM).

{{< include _show-table.qmd >}}
{{< include _bem-annual-betas.qmd >}}
{{< include _bem2-characteristics.qmd >}}

## Implementation

### Periodic Cross-Sectional Persistence {#annual-cross-sectional-persistence}

For a lag of $\tau$ years, match stocks by `permno` in years $t$ and $t+\tau$.
For each characteristic $X$, keep the set $\mathcal S_{t,\tau}$ of stocks with finite values of $X$ in both years.
Within this matched sample, winsorize each year's values separately at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles.
Using the winsorized values and their cross-sectional means, the Pearson correlation is

$$
\rho_{t,t+\tau}(X)=
\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i\in\mathcal S_{t,\tau}}
      (X_{i,t}-\bar X_t)(X_{i,t+\tau}-\bar X_{t+\tau})}
     {\displaystyle\sqrt{\sum_{i\in\mathcal S_{t,\tau}}(X_{i,t}-\bar X_t)^2}
                   \sqrt{\sum_{i\in\mathcal S_{t,\tau}}(X_{i,t+\tau}-\bar X_{t+\tau})^2}}.
$$ {#eq-bem4-periodic}

Shift the future year's join key back by the lag so that each stock's observation in $t+\tau$ joins its observation in $t$.
Use the same winsorized Pearson correlation as in @sec-bem-correlation.

```{python}
from _bem_monthly import winsorized_corr

measures = ["Beta", "Size", "BM"]
lags = range(1, 6)
characteristics = annual_panel.select("permno", "year", *measures)

def annual_persistence(lag):
    future = characteristics.with_columns(year=pl.col("year") - lag)
    return (
        characteristics.join(future, on=["permno", "year"], suffix="_future", validate="1:1")
        .group_by("year")
        .agg(
            winsorized_corr(pl.col(x), pl.col(f"{x}_future")).fill_nan(None).alias(x)
            for x in measures
        )
        .with_columns(pl.lit(lag).alias("Lag"))
    )

annual = pl.concat([annual_persistence(lag) for lag in lags]).sort("Lag", "year")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem4-annual
#| tbl-cap: Annual cross-sectional persistence of beta (BEM Table 4.1)
#| echo: false

beta_by_year = (
    annual.pivot(on="Lag", index="year", values="Beta", sort_columns=True)
    .sort("year")
    .rename({"year": "Year", **{str(lag): f"Lag {lag}" for lag in lags}})
)
show_table(beta_by_year)
```

The lags are in years.
The blank cells in @tbl-bem4-annual require a comparison year beyond 2012.
Of the 110 estimates, 107 agree with BEM to two decimal places and three differ by 0.01.
The companion plot in @fig-bem4-annual shows how much beta persistence varies across formation years, even at the same lag.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem4-annual
#| fig-cap: Annual persistence of beta by lag
#| fig-alt: Five lines show beta correlations by formation year. One-year correlations generally exceed the longer-lag correlations and are higher in the 2000s than in the early 1990s. Lines for longer lags end earlier.

from plotnine_polars import aes

(
    annual.with_columns(lag=pl.col("Lag").cast(pl.String))
    .ggplot(aes(x="year", y="Beta", color="lag", linetype="lag"))
    .geom_line()
    .scale_x_continuous(breaks=range(1988, 2013, 4))
    .scale_y_continuous(expand=(0, 0))
    .coord_cartesian(ylim=(0, 1))
    .scale_color_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2")
    .scale_linetype_manual(values=["solid", "dashed", "dashdot", "dotted", (0, (5, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2))])
    .labs(x="Formation year", y="Pearson correlation", color="Lag (years)", linetype="Lag (years)")
    .theme_minimal()
    .add_theme(figure_size=(8, 4), legend_position="top")
)
```

### Average Cross-Sectional Persistence {#average-across-years}

Give each formation year equal weight.
With $N$ years indexed from 1 through $N$, the average persistence at lag $\tau$ is

$$
\rho_\tau(X)=\frac{1}{N-\tau}\sum_{t=1}^{N-\tau}\rho_{t,t+\tau}(X).
$$ {#eq-bem4-average}

Here $N=25$, so the one-year estimate averages 24 correlations and the five-year estimate averages 20.
@tbl-bem4-beta reports the averages for beta and @tbl-bem4-characteristics puts all three characteristics side by side.

```{python}
average = annual.group_by("Lag").agg(pl.col(measures).mean()).sort("Lag")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem4-beta
#| tbl-cap: Average annual persistence of beta (BEM Table 4.2)
#| echo: false

show_table(pl.DataFrame({
    f"Lag {lag}": [beta] for lag, beta in average.select("Lag", "Beta").iter_rows()
}))
```

## Interpreting Persistence {#interpret-persistence}

Low beta persistence can reflect changing market exposures, noisy estimates, or both.
Overlapping estimation windows can raise the correlation because the two estimates use some of the same returns.
Here the December 12-month betas use daily returns from separate calendar years.
The set of stocks with valid measurements at both dates can also change with the lag, so differences across lags reflect both the time between measurements and the stocks observed at both dates.

## Presenting Persistence

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem4-characteristics
#| tbl-cap: Average persistence of beta, size, and book-to-market (BEM Table 4.3)
#| echo: false

show_table(average.rename({"Lag": "Lag (years)"}))
```

@fig-bem4-averages plots the averages from @tbl-bem4-characteristics.
Size is the most persistent characteristic at every lag.
Its average correlation falls from 0.96 at one year to 0.88 at five years.
At five years, beta and BM are at 0.42 and 0.47.
The size averages agree with BEM at the reported precision.
Beta's three-year average is 0.49 here and 0.48 in BEM, and the other beta averages agree.
BM correlations are 0.02 to 0.05 higher in this replication across the five lags.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem4-averages
#| fig-cap: Average persistence of beta, size, and book-to-market by lag
#| fig-alt: Average size persistence stays near 0.9. Book-to-market falls from 0.76 to 0.47 and beta from 0.61 to 0.42 between the one- and five-year lags.

(
    average.rename({"BM": "Book-to-market"})
    .unpivot(index="Lag", variable_name="characteristic", value_name="correlation")
    .with_columns(pl.col("characteristic").cast(pl.Enum(["Beta", "Size", "Book-to-market"])))
    .ggplot(aes(x="Lag", y="correlation", color="characteristic"))
    .geom_line()
    .geom_point(aes(shape="characteristic"))
    .scale_x_continuous(breaks=lags)
    .scale_y_continuous(expand=(0, 0))
    .coord_cartesian(ylim=(0, 1))
    .scale_color_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2")
    .scale_shape_manual(values=["o", "s", "^"])
    .labs(x="Lag (years)", y="Average Pearson correlation", color="", shape="")
    .theme_minimal()
    .add_theme(figure_size=(8, 4), legend_position="top")
)
```
